messages.reasoning_content:
Both fetched. Key findings:

Permissions doc (v24.21.0):
- "This feature does not protect against malicious code... Malicious code can bypass the permission model" — tenant isolation as sole boundary is wrong.
- Audit mode: does NOT deny; only publishes to diagnostics channel. Staging with --permission-audit is fine for discovery, but is not enforcement.
- Wildcards: "/home/*.js will work similar to /home/*" — after wildcard, subsequent chars ignored. So --allow-fs-read=/srv/jobs/*.js is effectively /srv/jobs/* — grants read to everything under /srv/jobs (and /srv/jobs itself treated as dir wildcard if exists).
- Directory auto-wildcard behavior.
- Symlinks: "Symbolic links will be followed even to locations outside granted paths. Relative symbolic links may allow access to arbitrary files" — must ensure no relative symlinks in granted paths. Job dirs may contain relative symlinks → conflict.
- Constraints: "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." Wait — but SECURITY.md says "Workers inherit the permission restrictions of their parent process." Conflicting evidence! The permissions doc constraint section says "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." That seems to be an older doc phrasing... In the fetched v24.21.0 permissions doc, constraints says "The model does not inherit to a worker thread." And SECURITY.md v24.21.0 says "Workers inherit the permission restrictions of their parent process. Passing an empty or modified execArgv to a worker does not grant it additional permissions." These conflict. The user asked: "If the sources do not establish one consistent worker-inheritance answer, state the limitation." So I should flag the conflict as UNVERIFIED / conflicting evidence. Actually the SECURITY.md statement is more recent/precise (about execArgv). The permissions doc constraint might be stale. But per instructions, state the limitation rather than choosing. I could optionally check the worker_threads doc page to resolve, but I have limited steps (used 1 of 8; tools available calls 1-7). Let me fetch the worker_threads doc page to check inheritance.

- --env-file: "not subject to the rules of the Permission Model" — reads env file before model init. Also env file outside read list — actually the constraint says env-file reads happen regardless, so it works, but it means env file bypass is intended; but for tenant isolation, env-file content becomes env vars readable by job code via process.env — cross-tenant secret exposure risk.
- Pre-opened FDs: "Using existing file descriptors via the node:fs module bypasses the Permission Model."
- process._debugProcess cross-process inspector — not gated; sandboxed process can force other Node processes on same host/user to open inspector. Requires OS-level isolation.
- --allow-worker enables worker_threads; combined with whatever inheritance behavior.
- node:sqlite bypasses fs permission model; Run-Time Loadable Extensions.
- Entrypoints automatically added to read list.
- drop() limitations; doesn't close already-open FDs.

Security policy: Node trusts code it runs; malicious code not in threat model; permission model is not security boundary; CWE-653 etc.
